Second Bail Application under Section 482 of The Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhia ("B.N.S.S.")
has been filed on behalf of the Applicant Lalit Kumar for grant of Anticipatory Bail in FIR No.0250/2025 under Sections 313/376/506 IPC, registered at PS: Badarpur, Delhi.

2. It is submitted that the Applicant is peace-loving and a law-abiding citizen, aged about 27 years,
having deep roots in the society.
He is currently working as a gym trainer in Palwal, Haryana and is sole bread earner of his family consisting of his parents and Wife.

3. It is submitted that there are frivolous allegations made by the Complainant against the Applicant, which have resulted in the registration of present FIR No.0250/2025 under Sections 313/376/506 IPC.
4. The facts in brief are that on 24.01.2021, Complainant and the Applicant met each other and soon thereafter, entered into a relationship.
Thereafter, on 24.06.2024, they met each other for the last time and mutually decided to part ways and end their relationship.

Even though, he was always ready and willing to marry the Complainant and had support of his family members.
5. Thereafter, the Applicants family members arranged his marriage and consequently, he got married on 10.02.2025.

Thereafter, on 28.02.2025, the Complaint was transferred to PS: Sangam Vihar, where also he joined the investigations.
Present FIR No.0250/2025
was registered on 26.05.2025 at PS: Badarpur, Delhi on false and frivolous Complaint filed by the Complainant.

6. It is asserted that the Applicant has been constantly harassed and having reasons to apprehend his arrest, he filed an Application under Section 482 B.N.S.S. before the learned ASJ for grant of Anticipatory Bail and he was granted Interim protection by the learned ASJ.
7. The Applicant tried to join investigations, but the IO never gave him chance to present true and correct facts and the evidence in his favour.

However, but the audio recording of the conversation between Complainants brother and the Applicant was provided wherein the Applicant was asked to break all forms of communication with the Complainant.
He also gave Screenshots of WhatsApp messages to the IO, which were sent to him.
8. Thereafter, on 17.07.2025, learned ASJ dismissed the Anticipatory Bail Application on the ground of gravity of offence.

9. The Applicant has filed present Bail Application on the ground that FIR is based on false,
concocted and fabricated story woven by the
This is a digitally signed order.

It is nothing but a well-hatched plan to implicate the Applicant.
The allegations made in the FIR are without any substantial proof or evidence of the alleged offence committed by the Applicant.
FIR has been registered with a single motive to harass and humiliate the Applicant.
No evidence has been produced on record to show that the Applicant is deliberately evading the investigation or has been threatening the Complainant.
10. In the Anticipatory Bail Application before the learned ASJ, the Complainant never contended even once that the Applicant had tried to approach, threaten or influence her.

The FIR has been registered with the intent to use it as an arm-twisting tactic for harassing and humiliating the Applicant, in order to damage his dignity, reputation and mental peace and also to seek revenge and settle scores for not being able to maintain a relationship for the reasons attributable solely to the Complainant.
11. Complaint filed by the Complainant, lacks any credibility.
Complainant states that she had filed several other Complaints, but all contained different versions of allegations and are contradictory.

It is contended that the Applicant had entered into a consensual relationship with the Complainant,
which turned sour and they became distant.
There is no criminality in the alleged acts, which merits invocation of criminal machinery.
It not only burdens that Court, but also blots the identity of the Applicant, on whom such allegations of heinous offence have been made.

sentences.text: The Apex Court has time and again made observations and warned against the misuse of the provisions, and has termed it a folly to treat each breach of promise to marry as a false promise, for prosecuting an accused for an offence under Section 376 IPC.
The consent, as defined under Section This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 10/10/2025 at 23:39:08 90 IPC, cannot be said to have been obtained under a misconception of fact.
It was a long-drawn relationship, implying consent, regardless of the desire of the parties to get married.
The Honble Supreme Court has held that relationship that lasted even for one year, is a good enough period to know whether the promise to marry is false or not.
13. It is also held by the Apex Court that it is inconceivable for the victim girl to keep meeting the accused or maintain a prolonged relationship with him, in the absence of consent on her part.

There is no material to substantiate "inducement or misrepresentation" on the part of the Applicant to secure consent of the Complainant for sexual relations without having any intention of fulfilling the promise of marriage.
14. In several cases, it has been held by the Apex Court that such lis amounts to an abuse of process of law and has deemed it fit to terminate the proceedings at the stage of Charge itself.

15. Furthermore, as per the Complaint, the alleged commission of offences by the Applicant occurred sometime on 28.06.2024, while the Complaint was registered after a gap of about 8-9 months, for which there is no explanation.
Such delay is a substantive factor to be considered in the Bail Application.

16. Furthermore, no detailed analysis of the evidence is merited at this stage and the Court need not to delve into the quality and quantity of evidence, but to see whether the accused person appears to have prima facie committed the offences as alleged.
The allegations of causing miscarriages without the consent of the Complainant, have been made.
However, it is submitted that in such a long consensual relationship, allegations of causing forced miscarriage is completely inconceivable.

She has produced somehow some questionable documents, the source of which has not been disclosed.
There is a presumption of innocence in favour of the Applicant at the pre-trial stage.
18. The Applicant has clean antecedents and has joined the investigation as and when directed by the IO.
He is a law abiding citizen with no criminal antecedents.

He is permanent resident of Palwal,
Haryana having strong community ties.

sentences.text: The denial of Bail or arresting the Applicant and sending him to jail would be counterproductive, in the present facts and circumstances.
He would also be denied access to lawyers and preparation of defence.
19. It is therefore, submitted that the Applicant may be granted bail.
20. Status Report has been filed on behalf of the State, wherein the details of the investigations carried out after registration of the FIR have been detailed.

It has been submitted that as per the Complainant, not only the Applicant caused miscarriages by giving abortion pills without the knowledge of the Complainant, but had also taken away approximately Rs.2,50,000/-, some gold jewellery and her ATM of PNB, which he has not returned.

The Applicant has got married to a girl,
who works in Delhi Civil Defence.
21. It is further submitted that during investigations, information was collected from the Hotel The Taj Oyo Hotel, Badarpur.
As per record of the Hotel, the Complainant and the Applicant had gone to the hotel together many times.
The Statement of the Prosecutrix was recorded under Section 183 BNS, 2023, which is in consonance with the Complaint as well as the This is a digitally signed order.

22.
The Anticipatory Bail Application was filed by the Applicant, during which he was given interim protection and he joined the investigations.
However, after dismissal of Anticipatory Bail Application on 17.07.205, he failed to join the investigations on 19.07.2025.
Raid was also conducted at his house on 23.07.2025, but he was not found available.
23. Considering the gravity of the allegations, the Bail Application is opposed.

Submissions heard and record perused.
24.
It is again one of the cases where the Complainant and the Applicant were in a consensual relationship since 2019 and continued for the about 6-7 years.

They used to go Hotel many a time,
where they established physical relationship.

It is claimed by the Complainant that the Applicant had made promise to marry her, but on 28.06.2024, he informed her that he wanted to quit from the relationship as his family members are getting him married to another girl and thereafter, he got married.
25.
It has been vehemently contended that the Complaints had been made earlier by the Complainant.
In one Complaint, which was filed in June, 2024, allegations of harassment on false promise of marriage were made.
Second Complaint dated 08.07.2024 was made with similar allegations.
Third Complaint was filed on 13.01.2025, wherein allegations of forced abortion without consent of the Complainant and taking away Rs.2,50,000/- and some gold jewellery, were made.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note from the aforesaid contentions of the Complainant that she knowingly and being aware of consequences of her act, continued her love relationship with the Applicant since 2019 and they This is a digitally signed order.

27.
There is no allegation in the Complaint that the Complainant was induced into this relationship on account of any false promise of marriage.
Eventually, the parties may have decided to get married, but it cannot be said that the sexual relationship was made on account of any promise of marriage.

It is also pertinent to note that as per the Complaint itself, Complainant was informed on 28.06.2024 by the Applicant that he intended to quit from their relationship and only thereafter,
various Complaints were filed by the Complainant.
The Applicant got married on 14.02.2025, after which the present FIR has been registered.

28. It is prima facie a case where voluntary consensual relationship entered into between the parties way back in the year 2019, which turned sour after about 6 years, resulting the registration of present FIR.
29. There is nothing to show that the Complainant was compelled to establish sexual relationship on any misconception of facts.
Pertinently, allegations have been made that many a time she got pregnant and the Applicant gave her abortion pills without her consent.
However, during the arguments it was stated that the abortion for the first time took place in the year 2021, then in 2022 and twice in 2024.
It is a matter of trial whether indeed any abortion was caused by the Applicant by administering pills, without her consent.

30 . It is also contended that Rs.2,50,000/- have been taken by the Applicant over a period of time and that gold chain, ring and ear-rings and ATM Card of PNB of the Complainant have also been retained by the Applicant, which he has not returned.
This again is a matter of trial.

The submissions and the Complaint reflect that the parties were in a voluntary consensual sexual relationship since 2019, which turned sour as the Applicant called quit the relationship in June,
2024 and got married with another girl on 14.02.2025, after which the spate of Complaints followed.
Considering the totality of the circumstances, it is a fit case for grant of Anticipatory Bail to the Applicant.

Therefore, the Applicant/Petitioner is admitted to Anticipatory Bail, subject to the following conditions:
